p: Funstation is a family arcade, so this is the colourful, noisy, tickets-and-prizes kind of place rather than anything aimed at adults. That makes it an easy win for a birthday treat or a school-holiday outing where the kids have been begging to do something. Agree a budget and a finishing time before you go in, and give each child their own amount on the card. It saves a lot of arguments at the prize counter and teaches a bit of planning along the way.

Star City itself sits in the Nechells area, close to junction 6 of the M6 and the famous Spaghetti Junction, which makes it easy to reach by car from across the West Midlands. The headline neighbour is the big Vue cinema, so a film followed by a session on the games is a classic combo, and the restaurants on site mean nobody has to go hungry.

A couple of practical pointers. School holidays and wet weekends bring the crowds, so a weekday or earlier visit is calmer if you've got little ones who don't like the hustle. Keep an eye on smaller children on the dodgems and around the busier games, and set a meeting point in case anyone wanders. If you're coming from the city centre, Star City is only a short drive out, so it's handy for combining with a trip into town for shopping, the canals around Brindleyplace or a museum visit.
